content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"API Documentation Generation and Publishing in Postman"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Clear, comprehensive API documentation is essential for developer adoption and successful integration. Postman simplifies this process by allowing you to automatically generate interactive documentation directly from your API collections and publish it to the web with minimal configuration."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Postman account with an active workspace."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"An existing Postman Collection containing requests, headers, query parameters, and descriptive examples."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enhancing Your Collection with Descriptions"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before generating documentation, ensure your collection is properly annotated. Postman uses Markdown to render descriptions for collections, folders, and individual requests. Click the edit icon next to your collection name or request to add context."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Authentication API\nThis collection handles user authentication operations such as login, token refresh, and logout."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Adding Request Examples"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Interactive documentation is most powerful when it includes realistic request and response examples. Users can see exact payloads and status codes."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Send a successful request in Postman to ensure you receive a valid response."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click \"Save Response\" and choose \"Save as example\"."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Name the example clearly (e.g., \"Successful Login\") and save it."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Generating and Viewing Documentation"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Postman generates documentation automatically as you update your collection. To view the generated documentation internally, click on your collection in the sidebar, navigate to the \"Overview\" tab on the right side of the screen, or click the \"View documentation\" icon."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Publishing to the Web"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"To share your documentation with external consumers, you must publish it to the Postman Public Network or a private custom URL."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click the three dots (...) next to your collection name in the sidebar."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select \"Publish documentation\" from the dropdown menu."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure your display settings, such as selecting an environment, choosing a custom domain, and styling the layout."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Click the \"Publish Collection\" button at the bottom of the configuration page."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Maintaining and Updating Published Docs"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Postman documentation updates dynamically. When you make changes to your collection (such as updating endpoints, adding parameters, or modifying examples), your published documentation updates automatically in real-time if configured correctly, ensuring consumers always see the latest specification."}]
